claims.text: Pulsed laser surface alloying at W–Cu interfaces will form a graded interfacial layer.
The laser-formed interfacial layer will prevent phase separation.
The laser-formed interfacial layer will prevent interfacial void formation.
Preventing phase separation and interfacial void formation will enhance the composite's thermal conductivity under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
Controlled pulsed laser irradiation at approximately 3–5 J/cm² with nanosecond pulses in an inert atmosphere is an applicable processing window.
Laser treatment will locally remelt and rapidly solidify the W–Cu interface.
Local remelting and rapid solidification will produce an interfacial layer enriched in both W and Cu.
The laser pulse will induce interdiffusion between W and Cu at the interface.
The resulting graded layer will eliminate abrupt compositional discontinuities at the interface.
The graded layer will suppress interfacial void formation during subsequent thermal and irradiation exposure.
The graded layer will inhibit phase separation during subsequent thermal and irradiation exposure.
Laser alloying will enhance bonding at the W–Cu interface.
Laser-treated composites will have higher effective thermal conductivity under service conditions than untreated composites.
Untreated W–Cu composites exhibit significant phase separation under operating conditions.
Untreated W–Cu composites exhibit significant interfacial void formation under operating conditions.
The intervention is applicable to composites containing pre-formed W ligaments in a Cu matrix.
The intervention is intended to remain effective during repeated heat-transfer cycles and irradiation relevant to W-based plasma-facing material/Cu-based cooling-component joints.
